en: Taal Volcano features Vulcan Point, a rare island situated within a crater lake on an island within a larger lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park contains one of the world's longest navigable underground rivers flowing directly into the sea.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash and gas that it temporarily cooled the entire global climate.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn cocoa-brown during the dry season.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected UNESCO World Heritage marine sanctuary located entirely in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The island province of Romblon is known as the Marble Capital of the Philippines due to its abundant, high-quality white marble quarries.
San Juanico Strait is the narrowest strait in the Philippines, separating the neighboring Visayan islands of Samar and Leyte.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon wind that brings dry, pleasant weather to the Philippines between November and February.
Mount Pulag, the highest peak in Luzon, is famous for its breathtaking sea of clouds that forms above its grassy summit.
Hinatuan's Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur is a remarkably deep, clear blue river that flows directly out of an underwater cave.
The small island province of Camiguin uniquely has more volcanoes, including the active Mount Hibok-Hibok, than it has municipalities.
The Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary in Mindanao is the largest freshwater swamp forest in the Philippines, providing a massive habitat for diverse wildlife.
